citations.claim: just before impact body approaches wall bottom at ~38 m/s with energy conserved near E0
one step later after wall contact velocity reversed and amplified to ~45 m/s despite e=0.1
first violating step: total energy jumps ~300J above allowed bound with zero controller work

counterfactual.change: moved wall x from 10.878 to 2.0 so body never hits wall; same 76 steps, no violation, proving wall impact causes energy gain

explanation: Body launched upward at ~38.4 m/s hits underside of thin static wall around step 76. Restitution e=0.1 should leave rebound speed ~3.8 m/s, but observed rebound is 45.2 m/s (faster than impact). With controller disabled (work 0) and gravity conservative, this ~300 J jump can only come from the contact solver: at high approach speed with tiny dt, impulse plus positional (Baumgarte) correction pushes the body out along the contact normal and adds velocity in the same direction as the bounce, injecting energy instead of dissipating it.
vision_note: A small blue body contacts the underside of a thin horizontal wall near the top center and remains pinned against it across steps 73 to 76 with almost no separation. No fast rebound away, penetration through the wall, or other large motion is visible within this window.
